newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS - Indexes quiet, skepticism is high.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS - Indexes quiet, skepticism is high.

text.p: Trading in major U.S. index options was moderate Thursday, with traders and investors showing some skepticism toward the market's strength.
By around 1340 CDT/1840 GMT, the blue chip Dow industrial average was up 12 points at about 6,825, well off its session high of 6,891.
The market was led by International Business Machines Corp, which surged 11-1/2 to 153-7/8 after reporting strong quarterly earnings late Wednesday.
"You'd think the market would be down a lot if it weren't for IBM," said one index options trader in Chicago.
"It makes you wonder," the trader said. "I'm wondering if we're not due for a bit of downward move here."
He said volatilities in OEX options were up slightly, one indication that investors may be expecting some downside.
The Chicago Board Options Exchange's volatility index, which is priced off certain S&P 100 index options, was up 0.15, or 0.70 percent, at 22.36. The VIX was up sharply Wednesday also.
The OEX was up about half a point at 756.48 and the S&P 500 index was down 0.70 at around 773. June S&P 500 futures were down 4.60 at 775.60.
Among OEX options, the May 740 put and May 760 call were the most active, with volume of nearly 5,600 and 5,200 contracts, respectively.
Other actives included the May 765 and 770 calls and the May 750, 755 and 760 puts.
By 1400 CDT/1900 GMT, total OEX put activity topped call activity by 41,168 to 30,236.
Among SPX options traded at the CBOE, put volume outpaced call volume by 29,314 to 14,874.
